name: User Logs
detail: Application and diagnostic logs stored by macOS. New logs are written as apps run; deleting these removes existing troubleshooting history.

name: Aerial Wallpapers
detail: The video wallpapers and screen savers macOS downloads on demand. Each one is fetched again the next time it is chosen, so this reclaims space rather than removing a choice.

name: Music Artwork
detail: Album and video artwork the Music and TV apps have downloaded. Refetched as you browse your library; nothing you own is stored here.

name: Desktop App Web Caches
detail: The web cache each Electron app keeps beside its data — Discord, Slack and the rest are browsers underneath. Refilled as the app is used, and separate from the accounts and messages it stores.

name: Desktop App Code Caches
detail: Compiled JavaScript and shader caches Chromium writes for Electron apps. Regenerated on the next launch, at the cost of one slower start.

name: App Update Downloads
detail: Installers that self-updating apps have already applied and left behind. Downloaded again only when the next update arrives.

name: Device Software Updates
detail: iPhone, iPad and iPod update images downloaded when you update or restore a device from this Mac. Each is several gigabytes and is fetched again if it is needed.

name: Dropbox Cache
detail: Copies Dropbox keeps of files it has recently synced. Rebuilt as syncing continues, and separate from the files in your Dropbox folder.

name: Google Drive Cache
detail: Content Google Drive has streamed or synced and kept locally. Re-downloaded on demand; files marked available offline are stored elsewhere.

name: OneDrive Cache
detail: Thumbnails and synced content OneDrive keeps locally. Rebuilt as syncing continues.

name: Spotify Cache
detail: Audio Spotify has buffered, including tracks downloaded for offline listening. Streams again over the network, so offline playlists have to re-download before they work away from a connection.

name: Crash Reports
detail: Diagnostic reports macOS wrote when an app quit unexpectedly. New ones are written as crashes happen; deleting these removes the history a developer would ask you for.

name: Saved Application State
detail: The windows and documents apps reopen with after a relaunch. Written again as you quit apps; clearing it means the next launch starts empty rather than where you left off.

name: Installers
detail: Disk images and packages sitting in Downloads. Each row shows when it arrived, so an installer you have already run is the one dated months ago; anything still wanted is downloaded again from where it came from.

name: Unfinished Downloads
detail: Downloads that were interrupted. Nothing can open a partial file; a browser starts again from the beginning rather than resuming these.
